thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PDR-98765 fired for hosts [gpu03, gpu04] in us-west-2-rack3 — symptom: KERNEL_OOPS -> kubelet NotReady (multiple nodes). Auto-escalation to eng-oncall. Link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PDR-98765

pagerduty-bot: Incident PDR-98765 created (priority: P1). Acknowledged: none yet.

sanjay: acked. I’m on it. tagging @maya for ops coordination.

maya: ack. seeing both hosts flapping in the infra dashboard, GPU host-level kernel oops + kubelet going NotReady. Likely same root cause, probably PCIe or nvme.

eli: quick check — are customer-facing pods scheduled on those nodes right now? can we evict/redirect?

sanjay: running `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu03` and gpu04 next.

maya: small subset of ML training jobs on gpu03, a couple of realtime inferencers on gpu04 (replicas). Starting cordon+drain on gpu04 to reduce customer impact.

sanjay: cordon/drain commands below:
```
kubectl cordon gpu04
kubectl drain gpu04 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
```

eli: connecting to serial for gpu03, pulling dmesg. attaching logs: `SERIAL://usw2-rack3-gpu03` — kernel shows XID 79 and then oops. collecting last 500 lines.

incident-bot: Attached runbook: https://confluence.example/runbooks/gpu-host-kernel-oops. Suggested next steps: collect serial logs, check nvme SMART, consider host reboot or RMA if persistent.

maya: drain finished on gpu04, pods rescheduled — monitoring for restarts failing (crashloop). so far ok.

sanjay: gpu03 still flapping, serial shows repeated kernel oops every ~90s. I’m going to isolate: cordon gpu03 and move remaining critical pods:
```
kubectl cordon gpu03
kubectl drain gpu03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=30
```

ops-lead: @sanjay @maya good call. This looks like a host-level failure rather than kubelet config. For now, prevent further scheduling across rack3 GPUs. I’m going to set a routing rule to avoid rack3 in the scheduler (temporary).

pagerduty-bot: PDR-98765 acknowledged by sanjay at 2025-11-12T18:12:23Z.

eli: nvme SMART shows reallocated sectors spike on gpu03, nvme errors preceding oops. opening an infra ticket for hardware RMA.

maya: are any customers affected? checking the customer-impact dashboard... one active customer job (cust-aml-42) lost a worker but autoscaled replica on another node picked up tasks. throughput dip ~12% in the last 10m for that tenant.

sanjay: updating status: incident status -> degraded for small subset of customers, no total outage. posting to #support with short note.

ops-lead: decision: short-term — cordon both gpu03/gpu04, perform host reboot on gpu03 once pods drained, place node under maintenance. Long-term — RMA gpu03 NVMe if reboots don't stabilize.

liam: (night on-call) I’m taking handoff at 18:24 UTC. summary: PDR-98765, two GPU hosts in rack3 kernel oops -> kubelet NotReady, gpu04 drained & healthy, gpu03 cordoned, serial logs show nvme errors, RMA ticket opened. Customer impact: small perf degradation for one customer; no 5xxs seen.

ops-lead: @liam thanks. next actions for night: 1) monitor gpu03 after reboot, 2) if oops persists, proceed with RMA, 3) keep support loop posted. escalate to platform oncall if more nodes in rack degrade.

liam: acknowledged handoff. I’ll pick up monitoring and post hourly updates. :white_check_mark:
